newsitem.title: USA: SEC charges against former Drexel trader dropped.
newsitem.headline: SEC charges against former Drexel trader dropped.

text.p: Charges made by the Securities and Exchange Commission against Warren Trepp, former head junk bond trader at the defunct Drexel Burnham Lambert, were dismissed Monday by an administrative law judge.
"The division did not meet its burden of proof in claiming that it exercised due diligence in discovering the cause of action at issue," wrote Carol Fox Foelak in her August 18 decision.

The SEC began proceedings against Trepp in 1995 in connection with a series of so-called parking transactions in 1986 between Drexel and its customer Reliance Group Holdings, an insurance holding company.

The agency alleged that an arrangement was reached between Reliance and Drexel's Beverly Hills, Calif., junk bond unit headed by Michael Milken, in which the insurance company sold selected bonds to Drexel and then repurchased them without suffering any losses.
Trepp carried out the arrangement on Drexel's side by selecting the bonds offered for sale, timing the sale and repurchases, the SEC alleged.

Although the administrative law judge found that Trepp was involved in the transactions, which led to the SEC's accusations of books and records violations, the judge ruled Trepp was "too remote from the scheme of causation" for more serious fraud charges made by the SEC.
